_comment: Eastern Cape Department of Education Grade 10 Accounting P1 (Financial Accounting), November 2018 provincial common examination.
Questions and marking-guideline answers extracted from the text layer of the official PDFs
(paper1.pdf, paper1_memo.pdf) and read against the rendered pages. The optional
'information' field (array of lines) carries the INFORMATION block of each main question; it is
attached to the FIRST sub-question of that main question and applies to all of its sub-questions.
The pre-printed ANSWER BOOK (paper1_answer_book.pdf) is tracked beside the paper.
memo_answer reproduces the marking guideline's figures and workings line by line (tick marks
removed; marking notes such as 'one part correct' kept). Unnumbered bullet sub-parts of a
question are kept in one entry with their marks added.
The paper's instruction table: Q1 Accounting Concepts and Accounting Equation 35 marks 30 min; Q2
Ethics, Internal Control and Wages Journal 35 marks 30 min; Q3 Notes to Financial Statements and
Balance Sheet 40 marks 30 min; Q4 Accounting Concepts and Analysis and Interpretation of Financial
Statements 40 marks 30 min; total 150 marks, 2 hours. A Grade 10 formula sheet is printed in the paper.
1.2 is one 30-mark table; the marks of each transaction (1.2.1-1.2.5) are counted from the ticks in
the marking guideline (5 + 4 + 8 + 4 + 9). In 2.3.3 the guideline's UIF amounts (95, 80, 70) are ten
times the 1% rate given in the paper; they are kept as printed and flagged in memo_note.

questions.context: QUESTION 1: ACCOUNTING CONCEPTS AND ACCOUNTING EQUATION (35 marks; 30 minutes) | 1.1 ACCOUNTING CONCEPTS. Choose the correct answer from the options provided. Write only the letter (A-D) next to the number (1.1.1-1.1.5) in the ANSWER BOOK.
questions.text: Telephone is a/an … account. A balance sheet B asset C expense D income
questions.memo_answer: C (expense)

questions.text: People who owe the business money are known as … A debtors. B creditors. C bankers. D wholesalers.
questions.memo_answer: A (debtors)

questions.text: Which of the following is not a non-current asset? A Land and buildings B Trading stock C Vehicles D Equipment
questions.memo_answer: B (Trading stock)

questions.text: Profits generated by the business will always increase … A owner’s equity. B assets. C creditors. D cash.
questions.memo_answer: A (owner’s equity)

questions.text: Which source document is used to record goods purchased on credit? A Original invoice B Duplicate invoice C Receipt D Cheque counterfoil

questions.context: 2.2 Read the paragraph, then answer the questions that follow. SMALL BUSINESS FAILING TO PAY A LIVING WAGE ‘More than a third of small businesses in South Africa pay their workers less than the minimum wage (as set by the government). This statement was based on inspections carried out at 1 744 workplaces in this sector, where compliance levels were found to be at 65%.’
questions.text: Why does the government set minimum wages?
questions.memo_answer:
Any relevant answer
• To protect the interests of the poor
• To reduce poverty

questions.text: Would you regard the actions of these small businesses as ethical? Motivate your answer.
questions.memo_answer:
No.
It is against the labour law.

questions.context: 2.3 INTERNAL CONTROL AND WAGES JOURNAL. Super Clean Cleaning Services is a small business that renders cleaning services to other businesses in the Nelson Mandela Metropole. Super Clean Cleaning Services recently received complaints from numerous clients. It is alleged that the cleaners frequently gather in the restroom to smoke and that their productivity is substandard.
questions.text: B Mills is frequently late for work and leaves early on a Friday. What steps should the owner of Super Clean Cleaning Services take to prevent this from becoming a habit of his staff?
questions.memo_answer:
Any relevant answer (excellent 3, good 2, fair 1):
• Supply each employee with a code of conduct
• Investigate the reason
• Give Mills a written warning

questions.text: Name TWO internal control measures that the owner of Super Clean Cleaning Services can implement in reaction to the complaints about smoking in public areas and poor productivity of his employees.
questions.memo_answer:
Any relevant answer
• Appoint a supervisor
• Convene a meeting with employees about the complaints
• Do regular spot checks at clients’ premises
